title: Why Orderliness Is A Predictor Of Classroom Management Success https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2024/03/07/orderliness-classroom-management-success/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin claims he can gauge a teacher's classroom management effectiveness within minutes of standing in their empty room, based purely on how orderly the physical space is, and explains the three underlying traits an orderly room reveals. A neat classroom signals an observant teacher able to detect misbehavior anywhere in the room, a detail-oriented teacher able to communicate precise behavioral boundaries, and a teacher who pursues excellence broadly, since 'how you do anything is how you do everything.' He acknowledges rare exceptions but insists that in the vast majority of cases, a disorganized classroom environment correlates directly with unhappy, distracted students and an overwhelmed teacher, positioning tidying the room as the single highest-leverage first step toward regaining control.
points: A teacher's classroom management effectiveness can reportedly be predicted just from the orderliness of their empty classroom, before ever seeing them teach.
An orderly classroom is linked to three underlying traits: being observant enough to catch misbehavior, being detail-oriented enough to communicate clear boundaries, and pursuing excellence broadly.
The principle 'how you do anything is how you do everything' is applied directly to classroom tidiness as a signal of a teacher's overall standards.
Tidying the classroom is presented as the single highest-leverage first step for a teacher trying to regain control of a struggling class.
quotes: I can tell how effective a teacher is before seeing them in action. I just need a few minutes in their empty classroom during a typical day.

These critical teacher characteristics are revealed in a pin-neat, well-organized classroom. They bode well for the teacher’s ability to supervise and see misbehavior whenever and wherever it happens.
If the environment displays excellence, so too does the teacher. They hold themselves to a high standard, which means they can’t help but to require the same of their students.
But 99 percent of the time a disorganized environment means unhappy, distracted students and a stressed-out teacher way in over their head.
Tidying up your classroom is the first and best thing you can do to begin gaining control and reversing the tension, bad behavior, low motivation, and poor work habits.
